solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Fish firm behind dock making a comeback (8)

indicatorNotes.behind: HARD goes after the other piece, so it sits behind it
indicatorNotes.making a comeback: coming back means running the word the other way

annotation.surface: A fish returns to its old dock, with a firm standing behind it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a harbour but is the verb to cut short, as a tail is docked.
annotation.definitionFit: A pilchard is a small oily fish of the herring family.

entries.clue: Academician entered secretly (2,6)

blocks.note: entered = came in, written here as IN CAME

annotation.surface: A member of the Royal Academy slips into a room unnoticed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Entered' has to be split into two words and put in the other order, which is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: In camera is the legal term for proceedings held in private, so it means secretly.

entries.clue: Thrill, not small, after PC taking million in damages (12)

indicatorNotes.not small: 'not' refuses the small, so S, its abbreviation, is dropped from the word
indicatorNotes.after: the thrill piece comes after the PC piece in the answer
indicatorNotes.taking: a thing taking something in holds it, so COP takes M inside

blocks.note: PC = police constable = COP, with M (million) inside
thrill = SENSATION, dropping its first S (small)

annotation.surface: A police constable, thrilled by the prospect, pockets a million in damages.
annotation.walkthrough: PC could be a computer, but here it is a police constable, the COP.
annotation.definitionFit: Damages awarded by a court are compensation for a loss.

entries.clue: In the East, Mike and sibling fare better than most? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a noun phrase: fare = food

indicatorNotes.In: M and BRO are placed in the word for the East

blocks.note: Mike is M in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Out in the East, Mike and his brother are doing better than most.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a verb (to get on) beside 'better than most', but it is a noun: food. 'In the East' reads as a location, yet it is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Ambrosia is the food of the gods, fare better than any mortal's; the question mark marks the playful description.

entries.clue: Arrogance said to develop: have row about that (7)

indicatorNotes.to develop: the letters of SAID develop into a new order
indicatorNotes.about: DIN goes about, around, the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: Someone warns that arrogance will grow unless there is a row about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with 'cow' here: a noisy quarrel, DIN. 'That' points back to the jumbled SAID.
annotation.definitionFit: Disdain is scornful arrogance toward others.

entries.clue: State after accepting request (6)

blocks.note: à la = after the style of, as in à la carte

annotation.surface: Someone states their position only after hearing a request.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' is not a placement word here but the French à la, 'in the manner of'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: Alaska is one of the fifty US states, the largest by area.

entries.clue: Bathing beach upper crust love (4)

blocks.note: a lid is the crust on top of something

annotation.surface: The upper classes love a day at the bathing beach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upper crust' reads as the posh set, but here it is a literal top layer, a lid.
annotation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air bathing place or beach.

entries.clue: Period ending this stretch in prison (8)

blocks.note: period here is the full stop, the mark that closes a written unit of words
a stretch is slang for a term served in jail

annotation.surface: A prisoner counts down to the day their stretch finally ends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Period' looks like a span of time to match the prison term, but it is the punctuation mark that ends a sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: A sentence both ends in a period and is a term served in prison.

entries.clue: One Scots smoker in queue to light up (8)

indicatorNotes.in: something placed in a word is put inside it, so LUM sits within LINE

blocks.note: lum is Scots for a chimney

annotation.surface: A Scotsman in a queue waits to light up his cigarette.
annotation.walkthrough: The smoker is not a person with a cigarette but a chimney, LUM in Scots dialect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: illumine is a literary form of illuminate, to shed light on.

entries.clue: Society combined with lowlife (4)

blocks.note: cum = combined with, as in kitchen-cum-dining room

annotation.surface: High society mixing with the lowlife.
annotation.walkthrough: CUM is the Latin 'with', used in English for a room or role that doubles as another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scum, the froth on a pond, is used for people thought worthless, just as lowlife is.

entries.clue: What describes ideal spot, as corrupt, tempter at last having entered? (8,4)

annotation.definition: What describes ideal spot, as corrupt, tempter at last having entered?

indicatorNotes.corrupt: the letters are corrupted into a new order
indicatorNotes.at last: take only the final letter of tempter
indicatorNotes.having entered: that R goes in among the letters

annotation.surface: Eden spoiled once the serpent slid in.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: Milton's epic tells how the ideal spot, Eden, was corrupted once Satan the tempter got in.
annotation.definitionFit: Paradise Lost is Milton's poem about the fall of Eden after Satan's entry.

entries.clue: Landlord old fellow collecting new desktop item (6,6)

blocks.note: a landlord lets property, so is a letter

annotation.surface: An elderly landlord picks up a new gadget for his desk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old fellow' looks like one phrase for an old man; it splits into O and PEER.
annotation.definitionFit: A letter opener is a blade kept on a desk for slitting envelopes.

entries.clue: Citrus fruit just turning on Aegean isle (6)

indicatorNotes.turning: a word turning faces the other way, so ON is read backwards

blocks.note: citrus fruit = LEMONS; this is its opening stretch
just = only: of LEMONS, only the ON flips
the last letter of LEMONS, left where it was

annotation.surface: Lemons ripening on a Greek island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' means only: of all LEMONS, just the ON turns, giving LEM-NO-S. 'On' looks like a link but is the part that flips.
annotation.definitionFit: Lemnos is a Greek island in the northern Aegean.

entries.clue: Inertia among rebel group without leader (8)

indicatorNotes.without leader: the first letter of FACTION goes

blocks.note: rebel group = FACTION, losing its F

annotation.surface: A leaderless band of rebels sinks into apathy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes sense of it: a faction with no leader does nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a state of not acting or moving.

entries.clue: Dreamy scientist has width for depth (7)

indicatorNotes.has: the scientist has, or takes on, a different letter
indicatorNotes.for: one thing given for another is a swap, so W goes where D was

annotation.surface: A physicist lost in thought measures the wrong dimension.
annotation.walkthrough: W and D are the standard abbreviations for width and depth; swap one for the other in FARADAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the adjective sense: a faraway look is abstracted, as if in a dream.

entries.clue: Novelist in apartment ringing taxi service (8)

indicatorNotes.ringing: FLAT forms a ring round UBER

annotation.surface: A writer at home in his flat phones for a cab.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' looks like making a phone call, but it means forming a ring around something.
annotation.definitionFit: Gustave Flaubert was the French novelist who wrote Madame Bovary.

entries.clue: Strength of attachment in enclave dissipated (7)

indicatorNotes.dissipated: the letters are scattered and reformed

annotation.surface: Loyalty in an isolated enclave slowly fades away.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is chemistry: valence measures an atom's power to bond with others.
annotation.definitionFit: Valence is the combining power of an atom, the strength of its attachment to others.

entries.clue: Arrogant show preceding fall — land here? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the place: somewhere you land

indicatorNotes.preceding: preceding means going before, so AIRS comes ahead of TRIP

blocks.note: putting on airs = an arrogant show

annotation.surface: Pride comes before a fall, and here is where you hit the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'pride comes before a fall'; the question mark flags that the definition only describes the place.
annotation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a strip of ground where aircraft land.

entries.clue: Church position allows in club practising abstinence (8)

indicatorNotes.allows in: to allow someone in is to admit them, so LIE admits BAT inside it

blocks.note: the lie of the land = its position

annotation.surface: The Church's stance lets abstainers into its club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society to join; it is the bat, placed inside LIE.
annotation.definitionFit: Celibate means abstaining from sex, so practising abstinence.

entries.clue: Ancient deity (answer beginning with E) (7)

indicatorNotes.with: with means accompanied by, so E is attached at the end

annotation.surface: A quiz asks for an ancient god, with the hint that the answer begins with E.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like a quizmaster's hint, but the answer begins with A, and E comes at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Astarte was the ancient Semitic goddess of fertility and war.

entries.clue: Raging hero to cool down in ebbing ocean (8)

indicatorNotes.in: to be in something is to be inside it, so CHILL sits within AES
indicatorNotes.ebbing: an ebbing tide flows back, so SEA runs backwards

annotation.surface: An angry warrior wades into the retreating sea to calm down.
annotation.walkthrough: The Iliad opens on the rage of Achilles, which makes 'raging' fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Achilles is the Greek hero whose wrath drives the Iliad.

entries.clue: Floor design (6)

annotation.definitionNote: Floor is the verb, to knock down: lay out

blocks.note: to floor someone is to knock them down flat, as a boxer does
design as a noun: the arrangement of parts on a page or plan

annotation.walkthrough: 'Floor design' reads as a floor plan, which is close to the second sense; the first is the verb, to floor a boxer.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: lay out is the boxing verb for knocking someone flat, and a layout is the arrangement or plan of a page or room.

entries.clue: Husband leaves part containing spicy grub (6)

indicatorNotes.leaves: one who leaves goes away, so H departs from HOT
indicatorNotes.containing: to contain is to hold within, so ROLE holds OT

blocks.note: a part in a play = role
H = husband, the letter that leaves

annotation.surface: A husband walks out partway through a spicy meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food to go with 'spicy', but it is the verb: to dig about.
annotation.definitionFit: To rootle is to grub about, rummaging as a pig does in soil.

entries.clue: Unknown actors in one club altered play structure (6,6)

indicatorNotes.in: placed in something is put inside it, so Y CAST goes into the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.altered: altered letters are changed in order

blocks.note: the actors in a play = cast

annotation.surface: Unfamiliar actors in a club put on a new kind of play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' reads as a drama to go with the actors, but here it is children's play.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: an inflatable castle children bounce on is a structure built for play.

entries.clue: Universal personal cover set up in part of US (4)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up means written upwards

annotation.surface: Someone buys universal cover for their belongings in a corner of America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Personal cover' sounds like insurance but is just a hat.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Utah is one state among the fifty, so a part of the US.

entries.clue: Ham producer with concern for animal welfare? (4)

annotation.definition: Ham producer with concern for animal welfare?

blocks.note: the surface reading is a pig farmer or curer of pork; the setter means a man who fathered a son named Ham
the surface suggests a humane farmer; the setter means the man who saved every species from the Flood

annotation.surface: A pig farmer who worries about the welfare of his animals.
annotation.walkthrough: Ham is Noah's son in Genesis, not pork, and the concern for animals is the ark he built to carry them two by two.
annotation.definitionFit: Noah was father of Ham and took the animals two by two into the ark.

entries.clue: Maybe book fair subject to further changes (8)

blocks.note: a book is, for example, a read

annotation.surface: A book fair's plans may change yet again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book fair' looks like one event; it splits into a read and 'just'. 'Maybe' marks the book as one example of a read.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to readjust is to adjust again, to make more changes to something.

entries.clue: Partner that was case manager for trader (8)

blocks.note: a former partner is an ex
a porter manages cases, carrying luggage

annotation.surface: A former partner once handled the cases for a trader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case manager' sounds like a lawyer or social worker; it is a luggage porter.
annotation.definitionFit: An exporter is a trader who sells goods abroad.
